english: Thus the field, the means of knowledge and the knowable have been told in brief; My bhakta (devotee), knowing this, becomes fit for mad-bhāva (My state). The means of knowledge were placed immediately after the modifications of the field, because they too are counted among those modifications. The knowable in its prabhāva (power) was placed immediately after the means, because the means are most needed to bring so unworldly a power within the understanding.
divergence_note: Read with Jayatīrtha's Prameyadīpikā on Madhva's bhāṣya (their 13.19): Madhva gives two compressed sentences about the order of topics: the means of knowledge were told first because they are included among the vikāra (modifications), and the prabhāva (power) came next because the means are many and of great use. Jayatīrtha unpacks both. On the first, he raises the objection that the means should come after Brahman is taught, since only then does one ask how to grasp it, and answers that they were stated right after the modifications, by way of upodghāta (introductory placement), to show that they belong among them. On the second, he asks why, against the order announced at 13.4, the knower's power was told before 'from what, what', and notes that number alone does not fix precedence (citing the maxim of the needle and the cauldron), so the real reason is usefulness: the means are badly needed to bring the alaukika (unworldly) power into understanding, but not to the same degree for the Lord as preraka (impeller), which is closer to ordinary experience and is taken up next. So the substance here comes from Jayatīrtha: the virtues listed as means fall on the field side, and the order of the chapter is set by what each topic needs from the reader. Neither commentator says anything on mad-bhakta or mad-bhāva, so 'My state' is left as the bare word; the other schools fill it as the state of the supreme self (Advaita), freedom from transmigration (Viśiṣṭādvaita), possessing My qualities (Śuddhādvaita), being Brahman (Bhakti) or liberation as supreme bliss (Advaita-bhakti), and no Dvaita counterpart is supplied for this verse.
everyday_application: Order a body of material by what each part needs from the reader: put the working methods right beside the problems they belong to, and put the hardest, least intuitive part immediately after the tools needed to grasp it. In an onboarding guide, the unintuitive architecture section should follow straight after the debugging and tracing tools that make it visible, while the obvious matter of who approves what can wait, because people pick it up from ordinary experience anyway.
